scientific_intent.scientific_task: Convolve a data sequence with a short kernel under XOR index addition using Walsh transforms.
scientific_intent.mathematical_operation: y[i]=sum_(j=0)^127 x[i XOR j]*k[j]; compute H((Hx).*(Hk)/N), with unnormalized naturally ordered Walsh-Hadamard H and H²=NI.
scientific_intent.discretization_or_topology: One65536-element Float32 sequence and128-element kernel padded with zeros to65536.
invariants: H²x=Nx and normalization applied in pointwise modulation.
Final XOR convolution agrees with independent direct sum for every output.
Kernel outside first128 entries is exactly zero.
accuracy_requirements: All65536 Float32 outputs exact on selected nonconstant dyadic fixture vs direct Float64 CPU sum and both references; original relativeL2<1e-6 also enforced; elementwiseatol1e-5.
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Float32 butterfly order and modulation association can round differently for general non-dyadic inputs; exact selected fixture does not prove all input distributions.
scientific_intent.input_size_regimes: log2N16,log2kernel7, one complete pipeline pertrial with input resets outside timer. Original log2N23 and random positive fixtures unmeasured.
scientific_intent.community_use_case: Source explicitly identifies generalized Fourier/Walsh transforms and electrical-engineering/numeric-theory applications, demonstrated through dyadic convolution; no specific scientific instrument or dataset.
scientific_intent.uncertainty: XOR-index convolution differs from ordinary shift-invariant spatial convolution; no physical signal or application accuracy requirement supplied.
